title: Prefill tokenization hotpath: microbatching, cache-sharding, and minimal-alloc parsing
text:
Prefill tokenization hotpath: microbatching, cache-sharding, and minimal-alloc parsing

description:
Goal: Reduce prefill-side CPU and wall-time overhead for common prompt patterns by introducing a microbatching tokenizer path, sharded prefix cache, and an allocation-minimizing ASCII/byte fast path. Motivation: tokenization and preprocessing are dominating short-request latency and blocking decode scheduling in our serving runtime for high QPS workloads (chat starters, short prompts). Target: 35-50% CPU reduction on median prefill requests; 10-20% overall end-to-end latency improvement for 1-32 token prompts under typical PLG traffic; 2-3x increase in tokenization throughput for concurrent short-prefill bursts.

background:
We currently run a general-purpose tokenizer on every prefill which does UTF-8 decoding, normalization, and allocation-heavy byte->codepoint->token pipeline. Observed hot spots: repeated substring lookups, transient string allocations per request, lock contention on a global prefix cache, and CPU branching in Unicode path for ASCII-dominant prompts. Related tickets: ENG-7241 explored a fast-path cache for some prefixes but left microbatching and cache sharding unresolved. This ticket focuses on the runtime-side changes needed to make prefill tokenization both lower-latency and lower-CPU without changing tokenization semantics.

acceptance_criteria:
New microbatch tokenizer path enabled behind flag: --tokenizer-hotpath=on
Median CPU time spent in tokenization prefill handler reduced >= 35% on benchmark suite (chat_starters, slack_bots) compared to baseline
End-to-end p50 latency for 1-32 token prefill requests reduced >= 10% under 95th percentile QPS load
No behavioral changes in token IDs for existing tests: tokenization unit tests pass (golden token streams)
Cache sharding avoids global lock contention: no central cache lock observed in flamegraphs under synthetic traffic
Documentation: runtime-1.20 release notes include opt-out flag and telemetry keys
Feature rollout plan: gradual enablement with telemetry gating and automatic rollback on error rate regression

implementation_notes:
Design a 2-path tokenizer: 1) ASCII/byte fast path using single-pass byte-level scanner that returns token IDs without heap allocations; 2) fallback to existing unicode-aware tokenizer for complex inputs
Introduce per-worker sharded prefix cache keyed by (model, tokenizer-version, tenant-hash) with LRU eviction — avoids global lock and reduces false sharing
Microbatching at prefill entry: coalesce up to N small prefill requests (configurable, default N=16) per worker into a single tokenizer invocation to amortize overhead on shared inputs
Expose metrics: tokenizer_prefill_cpu_ms, tokenizer_prefill_alloc_bytes, tokenizer_prefill_cache_hit_ratio, tokenizer_prefill_microbatch_size_histogram
Integrate with scheduler: ensure prefill microbatches are scheduled without delaying large prefill jobs; prefer deadline-first scheduling so long-running prefill ops don't starve decodes
Implement zero-copy views for text->byte mapping for download/serve paths to avoid duplicate string copies when building KV cache entries
Add coverage for multilingual prompts: ensure fallback branch exercised for non-ASCII inputs and measure cost delta
Provide compatibility layer for older tokenizer versions: cache namespace includes tokenizer-version to allow rolling upgrades without cache poisoning

tradeoffs_and_risks:
Microbatching can increase tail latency for single-request flows if not carefully scheduled; mitigated by deadline-first scheduler and small max-batch size
Fast-path for ASCII reduces allocations but requires careful correctness testing to ensure identical token IDs; risks subtle unicode edge-cases
Sharded caches reduce contention but increase aggregate memory footprint; need to tune per-shard capacity and eviction policy
Prefix caching could mask prompt changes leading to stale prefix reuse; we namespace caches by model+tokenizer-version+tenant to reduce cross-tenant contamination
Rolling rollout complexity: need telemetry to detect regressions rapidly and an automatic rollback hook tied into console rollout UI

benchmarks:
Baseline (mainline runtime-1.19 build): median tokenizer CPU per-prefill: 4.6ms; alloc 3.2KB; p50 end-to-end prefill latency (1-8 tokens): 9.8ms
Initial prototype (microbatch only): median tokenizer CPU: 2.9ms (-37%); alloc 2.0KB; end-to-end p50: 8.9ms (-9%)
Prototype with ASCII fast-path + sharded cache: tokenizer CPU 1.8ms (-61%); alloc 0.6KB; end-to-end p50: 7.3ms (-26%); cache hit ratio 72% on chat_starters dataset
Note: synthetic bootstrap benchmarks run on c5d.large workers with 8 threads; production numbers will differ — need canary runs

Design review: finalize API and cache sharding contract (owner: Ravi)
Implement microbatching scheduler + tokenization coalescer (owner: Eng-TokenTeam)
Implement ASCII fast-path tokenizer in C++ runtime with optional SIMD path (owner: Diego)
Add per-worker sharded cache and eviction telemetry (owner: SRE)
Add unit/integration tests and golden token fixtures across 30 languages (owner: QA)
Create canary jobs and dashboards in Console (owner: Observability)
Rollout plan and feature flag publish (owner: PM)
Post-deploy monitoring and rollback automation (owner: Reliability)
Documentation and changelog entry for runtime-1.20 (owner: Docs)
Security review: evaluate cache key material and tenant isolation (owner: Security)

notes:
2026-02-16: Triage meeting — labeled P1. Decided to prototype microbatcher first to validate scheduling tradeoffs.
2026-02-23: Design review — agreed on sharded cache keyed by tenant-hash. Action: SRE to estimate memory overhead per shard.
2026-03-02: Prototype implemented by Diego; initial benchmarks promising. PR opened (#4512).
2026-03-05: QA caught mismatch on token IDs for Unicode combining characters in ASCII fast-path; added extra checks and fallback to unicode tokenizer for these cases.
2026-03-09: Canary rollout started in us-west with 10% traffic. Early telemetry: 18% reduction in overall request CPU; no increase in error rates. Monitoring dashboards added.
Next steps: finish integration tests for multi-tenant cache namespace, finalize release notes, and schedule full rollout after two-week canary window.
